observation_summary: The type inference engine fails to correctly infer properties of an anonymous object when that object is passed as an argument to a function that expects a union type containing record types.
hypothesis: The type inference logic in PrototypeObjectType.matchConstraint only checks if the constraint is a record type directly, failing to handle cases where the constraint is a union type that contains record types as alternates.
prediction: The fix will involve adding logic to iterate through the alternates of a union type constraint and applying the record type matching logic to any record type found within the union.
experiment_rationale: The provided diff shows exactly this: an 'else if (constraint.isUnionType())' block was added to iterate through union alternates and call 'matchRecordTypeConstraint' on any record type found, confirming the hypothesis that the original algorithm was incomplete.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a failure in the computational logic of the type inference algorithm. It was not checking all possible types within a union constraint, which is a procedural oversight in the inference method. It is not a 'Checking' bug because it is not a missing guard on a value, but a missing step in the algorithm's traversal of type constraints. It is not 'Function/Class/Object' because it is a local procedural correction within an existing inference method.
evidence_used: The fix_diff_oracle shows the addition of a loop to iterate through union type alternates.
The failing tests indicate that record type inference fails specifically when union types are involved.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds a check (isUnionType), the root cause is the absence of the necessary algorithmic step to process union types, not a missing validation of input data.
This is a local algorithmic correction within an existing method, not a design-level capability gap.
